findings.summary: I read every required source in full, in Read calls of 120 lines or fewer, from the CODEX-02-C app-context directory: the engineering README, ENGINEERING_DESIGN_V1.md v1.2 (1–411), MODULE_GUIDE, REVIEW_NOTES, PRODUCT_V1 v0.4.1 (1–262), the whole of PROJECT_CONTEXT v1.94 (1–1294), AGENTS, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, GOVERNANCE, APPROVALS (APPROVAL-007) and SYNTHETIC_CONSENT_ONBOARDING_TRACK. The v1.94 change is only the DECISION-036 LLC/EIN filing record plus its header and changelog row, so no product, privacy, architecture or authorization input changed. I then checked the actual working-tree source at 5bd7d8b against the card and the 2026-11-12 instructions, and it conforms to engineering v1.2. Every operation runs inside the accepted withSession. The latest consent row is locked FOR UPDATE before any private rows (ADR-E02 and the WM-02 consent-before-child-write rule). The context fence and owned current-epoch membership both come before the scoped receipt lookup, and an exact receipt or an equivalent initial create returns before the CAS check or quota. Sibling creation is explicit, corrections append history under a CAS check, and data from a prior epoch makes setup unavailable (PD-003 and PD-014). Migration 008 uses ON DELETE CASCADE, rejects updates to history and receipts, and has a deferred check that each current profile matches a version row. The HTTP union and the allowlist for the two setup shell paths are scoped exactly. In the UI, a transient passive failure keeps the RAM-only pending command and the sticky error, and only a 403 or a changed context clears private intent. All three acceptance criteria are met with real evidence: the 67/67 suite, build, the full card checker including the protected child PG/HTTP probe, a real HTTP/React regression (a lost sibling acknowledgment, then a passive 503, then Retry with the same UUID adds no child or receipt), and native CUA covering all eight scenarios, including the held old private GET. Since the review2 pass on 832, the only changes are the trailing space removed from one test line (the test file now has no trailing whitespace), REPORT completion text and the status file; the eight UI/service/HTTP/migration source blobs the CUA record pins are byte-identical. Review2's nits about the completion record are addressed. 10-A/G-E03, the final real consent wording, retained-data review, providers and public access all remain closed and are not claimed resolved.

Delegated acceptance under LOOP-POLICY-001 must pin the exact reviewed and merged revision, the same point REVIEW_NOTES item 8 makes. findings.title: The 5bd CUA record reuses the 832 observations rather than a fresh rerun
findings.problem: The CUA record bound to 5bd states that the eight scenario observations were carried over from the 832 native run because all eight proof source blobs are identical. Only the expired-access fence was freshly re-inspected. The record discloses this, and it is justified because the only source change is whitespace in a test file that is not among the proof blobs. Still, it is not a full native rerun on 5bd.
findings.fix_check: No action needed beyond keeping the existing disclosure in the acceptance companion. If any UI, service, HTTP or migration blob changes before merge, run a fresh native eight-scenario pass.

findings.title: Constructor reads access.withSession without the accessor guard
findings.problem: The own-data guard rejects accessors on options and env without invoking them, but `access.withSession` is read through ordinary property access, so a getter on the access object would run. The access object is the trusted, accepted adult-access service, so the risk is minimal. The instructions' wording about rejecting accessors without invoking getters is stated for options and env, and the access object is not explicitly covered.
findings.fix_check: Optional: check that withSession is an own data property through Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor before using it, or document in CHILD_SETUP_CONTRACT.md that the trusted access object is outside the own-data guard.
